rationale: Every supplied artifact use of claim C-AIR2-001 consistently preserves its scope and limitations. The claim states that GA-ASI 'publicly describes a DAA architecture combining cooperative surveillance sources such as TCAS/ADS-B with an air-to-air radar for non-cooperative aircraft,' with a scope limited to 'GA-ASI vendor description; architecture claim only.' All uses in the artifacts explicitly refer to the 'vendor-described architecture' or 'public material' and include clear qualifiers such as 'not an authority record for a current TSO authorization,' 'vendor architecture does not prove performance or certification,' and 'Do not imply GA-ASI approval status beyond exact claims.' The artifacts also explicitly reject overstatements like 'GA-ASI is the only certified DAA system,' reinforcing the claim's boundaries.
